data.textDisplay: Thanks, Stephanie. You have been my undereye Guru for years, and I have learned a wide array of helpful tips from you over the years!

My best advice. Don’t use a 10x mirror. lol Just joking. I really struggle with concealer settling in my fine lines. Im 56. I started putting my eyeshadow primer on my under eyes very sparingly. Seems to help a bit. But for me it’s pat pat pat with my finger and then set very lightly with a fine setting powder. Then pat pat pat again. It never completely eliminates the settling, but eventually it looks okay enough.

Thank you SO VERY MUCH for this fantastic video, Stephanie!! The struggle has been SO REAL and I never had this problem a few years ago. I  have a huge collection of concealers (HUGE!) and turns out.. THEY weren't the problem! I also so appreciate you mentioning the difference with application techniques because I've bought concealer brushes and have tried using them thinking that's what I supposed to do but it looks worse.
This video with all your knowledge, tips & techniques is LIFE-CHANGING and I'm so thankful you made this!! ❤
I do use a brush at first but then I always go back in with my finger. It just blends better, I totally agree
I got the Wet n Wild pink powder and few days ago and it is wonderfully under my eyes.

As a dry skinned, *older person, this is definitely a struggle. One product I will repurchase and always have on hand is the BB vitamin enriched Eye Base. I find that it preps my parchment paper dry and thin inner under eye area beautifully but also— if I mess everything up with powder, a tiny dab will smooth it back out. It’s pricey, but I use the tiniest bit for each eye. I’d rather have some natural luminosity to that area than any messes I make with powder, if I’ve made a mess.

I had to feedback! I used my finger for my corrector (Huda) and concealer (Nars) then set with my newly purchased Pat McGrath and so far wow! It’s stayed put, no cakey mess and isn’t drying. 
Oh and I got the wet n wild stick to swipe before applying. 🎉🎉🎉🎉🎉

I’ve tried so many combos/techniques under eyes and always creased.  Eye creams either disappear or mottled my concealer.  Saw another influencer recommend tiny bit of Vaseline under eye; then apply corrector/concealer/powder light layers with finger.  Never thought it would work but it did!  I still get small amount of creasing after few hrs but just dab with finger and smooths right out.  Best I’ve been able to find thus far.  Yours looks fab!

Wow is that first product expensive!! I thought it said $88 but I need new glasses and when I clicked on it is $188. Thats definitely out of my price range. Even 20% off puts it over $150. Oh well. Needing new glasses and contacts is expensive so maybe some other time you can remind us about that product. Did just get the Murad that was half off at Ulta from your recommendation so I’ll just go with that for now.

Thanks for sharing your techniques. 
I'm grateful you're here !

This has been such a game changer video for me to watch on how to apply my concealer. Thank you for posting this video. Some of is “aged” ladies out here need to see other methods to apply our concealer and not look so dry.
Concealer and fingers work just fine👍
Needed to see this. Once again I trust you and Risa on u tube. You truly are the best.

This was incredibly helpful especially the skin prep you do prior to going in to conceal under eyes . and thank you for listing all your skin care product options! You always have helpful, doable techniques. I have terribly dry wrinkled dark under eyes so I’m crossing my fingers your recommendations and technique will help

I agree with you about the brush.  Applying concealer with my finger always looks better.  I love the Pat McGrath Under Eye pressed pink powder.  It’s so smoothing and brightening!  I apply it with a Real Techniques mini concealer puff because even applying powder under my eyes with a brush looks dry on me.
Thank you you’re the only one who seems to get the under eye issue!
Thank you, Stephanie! I learn so much from the detailed  recommendations you share about all things beauty—  for mature skin!
You continue to be my undereye expert!

Hi Stephanie as someone who has severely dry rosacea and eczema prone skin moisturising the undereye is the most important thing.  I don't use a stick but I do use a decent layer of a second eye cream that has a little bit of dimethicone and a peach tint.  I'm currently using the Zelens eye cream as my actual skincare and the olay eye cream as my primer (the olay has a peachy tint and a little bit of dimethicone).  I give it a few minutes to settle while I apply my primers and my eyeshadow (any fallout is caught by the eye cream and can be easily dealt with).  I have tried sticks but prefer the cream.  I have been doing this a very very long time and long long before lip balms etc became trendy.  For a long time I used the First aid beauty niacinamide eye cream, but the olay is similar and more affordable.  Best wishes x
Thank you Stephanie; always appreciate the way you explain skincare. I always look for ceramides & peptides in my skincare.
